correctness.rationale: The claim is reduced to exact polynomial identities from the published quartic. The normalized Hessian resultant is \(729x^3(x^3-3x+1)^6(106x^3+3x^2-6x-2)\); a residual Gröbner basis gives \(106x^2+23x+19y+3=0\); there are no Hessian intersections at infinity; the two \(x=0\) tangent contacts are exactly three and four; and the residual cubic is squarefree, irreducible, and has discriminant \(-1026^2\). The packaged checker replays all of these identities exactly.

value.rationale: This is the complete exact arithmetic description of a canonical Weierstrass divisor on the irreducible cusp fiber of a sporadic genus-three Teichmüller curve, replacing the only numerical step in the published t=1 flex census. The residual cubic is intrinsically selected by the canonical Hessian intersection, not by an arbitrary slice, and its irreducibility and Galois structure provide reusable exact data for symbolic and arithmetic study of this degeneration.
